quickAnswer: Periodic restoration and refinishing for commercial lobby marble, granite, and travertine costs between $1.85 and $6.50 per square foot as a standalone project, depending on whether the stone needs light diamond-pad burnishing, multi-grit wet honing, travertine void filling, or deep lippage grinding. blocks.text: Why Daily Mopping Cannot Prevent Traffic-Lane Dulling on Natural Stone

No matter how diligently your night crew dust-mops and damp-mops a marble or travertine lobby, high-volume pivot zones—immediately inside revolving doors, in front of the security concierge desk, and at elevator call buttons—gradually lose their reflectivity. Unlike Vinyl Composition Tile (VCT), where foot traffic wears down a sacrificial acrylic wax coat that can be chemically stripped and recoated overnight, natural stone polish is mechanical rather than topical. The mirror sheen on Calacatta marble or Venetian travertine comes from light reflecting off tightly aligned microscopic mineral crystals.

Over 6 to 12 months of commercial foot traffic, fine silica grit fractures the peaks of those calcium carbonate or quartz crystals, scattering reflected light and creating a cloudy, washed-out path known as traffic-lane greying. Restoring optical depth requires mechanical resurfacing with industrial diamond abrasives, oxalic or aluminum-oxide polishing compounds, and subsurface fluorochemical or siloxane impregnating sealers billed at specialty labor rates of $55 to $95 per hour.

blocks.title: Never Allow Vendors to Apply Acrylic VCT Wax to Marble or Travertine
blocks.text: Unqualified janitorial contractors sometimes attempt to hide dull marble by applying acrylic VCT floor finish ('wax'). Because natural stone breathes moisture vapor from the concrete subfloor slab, topical acrylic coatings trap sub-slab humidity, causing the stone to spall, yellow, and flake within months. Stripping unauthorized acrylic wax off etched marble with alkaline strippers adds $1.25 to $2.00 per square foot to restoration invoices.
Commercial Stone Restoration & Refinishing Price Matrix (Per Sq Ft)

Stone restoration pricing scales directly with the number of mechanical diamond grit stages required to remove surface scratches, acid etch marks, and uneven tile edges (lippage). A quarterly maintenance buff using diamond-impregnated pads (DIPs) is fast and economical, whereas full multi-stage wet diamond grinding after years of neglect is a capital-intensive intervention.

blocks.text: Note that when facility managers elect the standard Quarterly Deep Floor Care add-on ($0.03 to $0.06 per square foot per month across the building's total rentable area), the contractor uses that monthly reserve pool to perform high-grit diamond pad maintenance in the stone lobby while simultaneously conducting hot-water carpet extraction on upper-floor corridors and walk-off mats.
Integrating Walk-Off Mat Extraction & Adjacent Restroom Threshold Protection

The single highest-ROI component of a quarterly stone restoration program doesn't actually touch the stone: it is the deep hot-water extraction of the lobby's recessed walk-off carpet grates, elevator cab carpets, and oversized entrance runners. Once entrance mats become saturated with winter ice-melt chlorides and silica sand, every pedestrian step transfers abrasive paste directly onto the freshly polished marble.

During quarterly restoration weekends, crews deploy commercial extractors such as the Sandia Sniper 6-Gallon Heated Carpet Extractor (100 PSI solution pump, dual vacuum motors, and a 2000W inline heater) or compact maneuverable units like the Rug Doctor Mighty Pro X3 Commercial Carpet Cleaner (28 PSI pump, vibrating agitation brush, and 3.9-gallon recovery tank) to flush embedded grit out of lobby runners and elevator thresholds before diamond-honing the stone.

Similarly, another frequent zone of accelerated marble etching is the transition threshold connecting the main stone lobby to ground-floor common restrooms ($15 to $30 per visit routine restroom fee). Acidic urine splash tracked on shoe soles from men's restrooms chemically burns calcite marble within feet of the restroom door. Installing enzymatic splash-control fixtures like Fresh Products Wave 3D Urinal Deodorizer Screens (10-box, 30-day enzymatic bacterial odor control with patented anti-splash post geometry) inside adjacent lobby restrooms dramatically reduces acidic shoe-sole tracking onto polished stone corridors.
Step-by-Step Scope of Work for an Annual Wet Diamond Honing Shutdown

When your lobby exhibits deep scratches, acid rings around planter pots, or hollowed-out travertine cavities, a light buffing pad will not solve the problem. Here is the five-stage workflow your restoration contractor should execute over a Friday-night-to-Sunday weekend shutdown:

items.name: 1. Masking, Baseboard taping & Architectural Metal Shielding
items.text: Technicians tape off 12 inches of dry-wall, wood wainscoting, brushed stainless elevator doors, and brass thresholds using waterproof plastic sheeting. Diamond honing produces an alkaline calcium-rich wet slurry that can stain anodized aluminum or fabric wall coverings if splash guards fail.

items.name: 2. Travertine Cavities & Grout Joint Repair
items.text: On travertine slabs, technicians inspect for collapsed factory fill pockets. Voids are flushed clean, dried with heat guns, and patched using color-matched polyester stone resin or polymer-modified unsanded travertine filler troweled flush with the floor plane.

items.name: 3. Progressive Wet Diamond Honing (100, 200, 400, 800 Grit)
items.text: Using a weighted 175 RPM planetary machine equipped with resin-bond diamond pucks and a water feed, technicians make slow criss-cross passes at 100 or 200 grit to level micro-scratches and erase chemical etching. After wet-vacuuming the slurry between every stage, they progress through 400 and 800 grit to establish a uniform, velvet-smooth honed finish.

items.name: 4. Mechanical Polishing (1,500 to 3,000 Grit) or Compound Buffing
items.text: If the design specification calls for a high-gloss architectural finish rather than a matte honed look, technicians step up to 1,500 and 3,000 grit diamond pads, finishing with a 5-micron aluminum-oxide or tin-oxide polishing powder under a natural hog's-hair pad to achieve a 85+ GU (Gloss Unit) mirror reading.

items.name: 5. Subsurface Impregnating Sealer & 24-Hour Cure Verification
items.text: Once the stone is thoroughly rinsed and dried to below 4% moisture content, technicians apply a breathable penetrating fluoropolymer or silane/siloxane sealer. Unlike surface coatings, an impregnating sealer lines the subsurface capillary pores below the wear plane, giving day porters a 15-to-30-minute reaction window to wipe up oil or coffee spills before staining occurs.

blocks.text: How to Evaluate Lump-Sum Restoration Bids vs. Amortized Contracts
Property managers generally choose between two procurement models for periodic stone maintenance:

items: Amortized Quarterly Deep Floor Program ($0.03 – $0.06/sq ft/month facility-wide): Best for stabilized multi-tenant buildings where consistent monthly CAM billing is preferred. Ensure the contract explicitly states how many square feet of stone lobby will be diamond-burnished each quarter so the contractor cannot skip quarters while still collecting the monthly fee.

On-Demand Specialty Work Order ($1.85 – $4.85/sq ft per event): Best for owner-occupied corporate headquarters or buildings hiring an independent Certified Stone and Tile PRO (install/restoration specialist) separate from their nightly cleaning vendor. Always require a 25-square-foot mock-up test patch in a conspicuous traffic lane before authorizing full lobby billing.

Gloss-Meter & COF Acceptance Criteria: Require the contractor to measure floor reflectivity with a digital 60-degree gloss meter and wet Static Coefficient of Friction (SCOF >= 0.42 DCOF under ANSI A326.3) before and after refinishing to verify slip-resistance compliance.

blocks.title: OSHA Silica Rule (29 CFR 1926.1153) & Wet Slurry Disposal
blocks.text: Dry grinding granite or siliceous stone generates respirable crystalline silica dust regulated by OSHA. Always mandate wet diamond honing methods indoors, and verify that your contractor collects all stone slurry via industrial wet vacuums for off-site disposal rather than dumping calcium carbonate paste down lobby floor drains, where it hardens like cement inside cast-iron traps.

faqs.q: What is the difference between marble diamond honing and crystallization (vitrification)?
faqs.a: Diamond honing is a purely mechanical process using water and progressive diamond abrasive pads (100 to 3,000 grit) to physically level scratches and polish the natural calcium carbonate crystal. Crystallization (vitrification) sprays a weak fluorosilicate acid solution onto the marble and buffs it with a steel-wool pad, creating a chemical reaction that forms a thin, hard calcium-fluorosilicate crust. Many architectural stone consultants prefer mechanical diamond polishing because excessive crystallization can darken grout lines and block subsurface moisture vapor transmission if over-applied.

faqs.q: How often should a commercial travertine or marble lobby be sealed?
faqs.a: In high-traffic Class A office lobbies cleaned 5x to 7x weekly (21.65 to 30.33 visits/month), water-based or solvent-based penetrating impregnating sealers should be tested every 6 months using a simple 15-minute water-drop absorption test and reapplied every 12 to 18 months. Remember that impregnating sealers prevent liquid absorption and staining, not acid etching or physical scratching.

faqs.q: Why doesn't granite need restoration as frequently as marble or travertine?
faqs.a: Granite is an igneous silicate rock ranking 6.0 to 6.5 on the Mohs scale, making it nearly twice as hard as calcitic marble or travertine (3.0 to 4.0 Mohs) and chemically inert to mild organic acids. While marble lobbies typically require quarterly or semi-annual maintenance polishing, a granite lobby often only needs annual deep rotary scrubbing, grout extraction, and diamond burnishing every 3 to 5 years.

faqs.q: Can our regular night janitorial crew perform diamond honing on the lobby?
faqs.a: Only if the vendor deploys a trained specialty floor tech division ($55 to $95/hour benchmark). Standard general cleaners ($35 to $65/hour) rarely carry multi-grit planetary diamond tooling or understand how to feather transitions between traffic lanes and perimeter walls without leaving visible swirl marks or burning the stone.
